meta.title: Warframe Overlay on Steam Deck: Reward Prices · FrameSight
meta.description: One AppImage in Desktop Mode puts platinum and ducat values on Warframe's reward screen at the Deck's 1280×800. Free, open source, no Overwolf.

card: One AppImage in Desktop Mode, and the reward screen read at the Deck's 1280×800.

hero.title: Relic reward prices on the Steam Deck.
hero.lede: Warframe runs on the Steam Deck through Proton. FrameSight runs beside it as a single AppImage in Desktop Mode, and reads the reward screen at the Deck's own 1280×800.

setup.title: Set it up
setup.step1: Switch to Desktop Mode: press the Steam button, open Power, then choose Switch to Desktop.
setup.step2: Download the AppImage from the latest release with the browser (the button below).
setup.step3: Make it runnable, from Dolphin (right-click, Properties, Permissions, Is executable) or from Konsole in your Downloads folder, then start it:
setup.step4: Choose an access level when FrameSight opens, then start Warframe from Steam.
setup.step5: In Warframe's options, set Display Mode to Borderless, so the overlay can draw over the game.

works.title: What to expect on the Deck
works.screenText: Warframe scales its HUD with the screen's height. The Deck's 16:10 has its own capture reference, so the cards are read where the game draws them.
works.modeText: FrameSight is installed and run in Desktop Mode, where Warframe and the overlay share the KDE desktop.
works.appText: Dashboard timers, the priced collection, mastery and warframe.market orders, on the same screen you play on.

items.q: Does it work in Game Mode?
items.a: This guide covers Desktop Mode, where FrameSight is installed and run. Game Mode runs games inside Gamescope, Valve's own compositor, and the overlay is not documented there yet.

items.q: Why the AppImage and not the Arch package?
items.a: Installing the package with makepkg needs SteamOS's read-only system unlocked, and a system update undoes it. The AppImage is a single file in your home folder that updates survive.

items.q: Does it slow the game down?
items.a: The overlay waits for the reward screen's line in EE.log before it reads the screen, instead of capturing all mission long.

items.q: Is the Deck's screen too small for the slips?
items.a: The slips are measured on the game's own layout and scale with it, so they line up under the cards at 1280×800.
